pr_title: Fix code editor moving lines without selected characters
pr_body:
Fixes #54362
Supersedes #54392

When the selection ends at the start of new line, move_lines_up/down shouldn't affect that line.

A question was raised in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/54392#pullrequestreview-796888504, if line should be moved when the selection covers only carriage return of a line. As an answer @jmb462 noticed that there's a visual difference, which could warrant different behaviour. I opened an issue to fix peculiar and ambiguous selection visuals: #72265
This pr handles the problem in line with other code editors, so that only selections ending at new line will be affected.
pr_comments:
Delete Lines is outlier not only by behaviour, but the default hotkey is strange as well. I wonder why it isn't `shift+delete` as in lot of other editors (refer VS Code, Visual Studio)? I had already forgotten this, because I changed it 2 years ago and haven't looked back 😄  EDIT: Ah yes, `shift+delete` is by default cut. I recall having that problem of changing the contents of clipboard when I wanted to delete some lines. It seems that Notepad++ defaults to `shift+delete` being cut as well. Well, each to their own, it's not a real issue since it's customizable.
I might look at that as well, however I think it's better to open another issue/pr for that?

issue_context.title: CodeTextEditor.move_lines_up moves an extra line when the selection ends at new line
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

Godot_v3.4-rc2 (or any other)

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

In script editor, when selecting lines either with shift+arrows or mouse and moving them with alt+up/down moves extra line at the end. This happens if the caret is on that line, even if no letters are selected on that line. In other popular editors I've used, only lines with selected letters are moved (Visual Studio, VS Code, Notepad++).
![extra_line](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1621768/139333417-c526348d-dec6-4b8f-8a64-6da2be97eea4.png)
If this is intended behaviour, I'm sorry and I'll go make a feature request instead...

### Steps to reproduce

Open script editor
Press shift+down
Press alt+up

### Minimal reproduction project

_No response_
comments: The most awkward situation this comes up if you paste multiple lines of code and want to move them - you almost certainly end up moving one more line than you pasted, since the caret ends up on that line.

review_comments: One potential pain point here is that there's 3 lines in a row which check for `text_editor->has_selection(c_next)`. Should they be merged into one `if` clause instead, same way as above (lines 1314-1324)? The resulting code would be of course a few good lines longer, but not necessarily any clearer.
